title: Cisco ISE Restore Audit and Configuration-Drift Detection Post-Restore
exclusions: Covers the detection logic documented for 'Cisco ISE Restore Audit and Configuration-Drift Detection Post-Restore' only. Does not replace full NAC policy design or firewall rule authoring or regulatory attestation. Entities listed in `network_exception_register.csv` during approved tests are excluded.
evidence: Saved search `network_cisco_ise_restore_audit_and_configuration_drift_` (UC-17.1.48), SOC dashboard panel "Network — Cisco ISE Restore Audit and Configuration-Drift Detection Post-Restore", and weekly export to `index=audit_evidence` sourcetype=csv:network_controls.

compliance.assurance_rationale: PCI 10.2 audit trails — restore events are auditable system actions.
SOX-ITGC change management — restore is a change requiring audit.
Art.21(2)(c) — restore is part of backup/restore lifecycle.
CP-10 (System Recovery and Reconstitution) — restore evidence.
compliance.controlObjective: Continuity-of-operations evidence for ISE backup-and-restore readiness.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Ingest synthetic events into `index=nac` sourcetype='cisco:ise:syslog' that satisfy the UC-17.1.48 SPL filters for 'Cisco ISE Restore Audit and Configuration-Drift Detection Post-Restore'. Run the saved search and confirm at least one alertable row with expected fields populated.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Ingest benign `nac` / `cisco:ise:syslog` events outside the detection threshold, or exclude the test entity via `network_exception_register.csv` with a valid window. Confirm zero alert rows for UC-17.1.48.

dataSources: ISE syslog `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog` *Administrative and Operational Audit* category — restore codes `51040` (restore initiated), `51041` (restore completed), `51042` (restore failed), `51043` (restore partial), `51044` (post-restore replication mismatch). Fields: `restore_source`, `triggered_by`, `restore_type` (config|operational|standalone). Combined with the ISE config-export feed: an OpenAPI poller dumps the active policy set (`/api/v1/authz-policy`, `/api/v1/identity-store`) every 1h and writes to `index=nac sourcetype=cisco:ise:config_export`.
spl:
(index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode IN (51040, 51041, 51042, 51043, 51044))
  OR (index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:config_export")
| stats count latest(_time) as last_event values(triggered_by) as admins by restore_type, MessageCode
| where count > 0
description: Audits all ISE restore operations (rare but high-impact events) and detects config drift in the immediate post-restore window — symptoms of an incomplete restore or a configuration roll-back gone wrong.
value: Restoring ISE from backup is a high-risk operation; it overwrites current policies with the policies from the backup snapshot. Any in-flight policy work between the backup time and the restore time is lost. This UC ensures every restore is audited in real time and triggers a config-drift comparison against pre-restore state to surface unexpected loss.
implementation: Confirm *Administrative and Operational Audit* category at INFO. The config-export OpenAPI poller is required for the drift comparison. Schedule the search every 30 min, search window `-4h@h to @h`, trigger on count > 0 (any restore event is alert-worthy).
visualization: (1) Audit table: restore events last 365d. (2) Diff panel post-restore: count of authz rules changed, identity stores reconfigured, certs replaced.

references.title: Cisco ISE 3.4 Admin Guide — Backup and Restore

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Certificate or EAP profile rollout** — Clients fail EAP-TLS during staged cert deployment for 'Cisco ISE Restore Audit and Configuration-Drift Detection Post-Restore'. Cross-check `FailureReason` and CMDB cert expiry.

2. **RADIUS/PSN maintenance restart** — Short auth failure burst while ISE node restarts. Match change window on `index=changes`.

3. **Guest or IoT onboarding surge** — Legitimate MAC registration spike skews `index=nac` `cisco:ise:syslog` baselines.

4. **Approved pen-test or scanner traffic** — Red-team exercises from netblock in `approved_scanners.csv` mimic auth failures.

**Suppression mechanism:** `network_exception_register.csv` keyed on `CallingStationID`, `NAS-IP-Address`, `valid_until`.
mitreAttack: N/A (platform lifecycle — ISE restore drill validation, no adversary technique)
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Same as UC-17.1.47.
• Config-export poller deployed.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
Double-check *Administrative and Operational Audit* INFO. Deploy config-export poller.

Step 2 — Create the search
Search in `spl` field. Schedule every 30 min.

Step 3 — Validate
Provoke a lab restore.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Dashboard "ISE — Restore Audit":
• 365-day audit log table.
• Drift diff panel post-restore.

Notification: Slack to `#ise-platform` on any restore event.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• **Restore initiated but no completion event** — Restore in progress; large operational-data restores can take 30–60 min.
• **Drift panel shows huge diff** — Backup was significantly older than current state; coordinate with the change team to reapply lost changes.
• **`triggered_by` empty** — Restore was triggered via CLI; admin user not captured in syslog. Cross-reference with shell login records.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk Add-on for Cisco Identity Services` ([Splunkbase 1915](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/1915)).). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog, cisco:ise:config_export into nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`MessageCode, restore_type`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: If someone restores ISE from a safety copy — like rolling back to last week's notebook — we record exactly what happened so we know what was kept and what was lost.
